intro: As a company grows, generic tools start dictating how the team works: fields that don't exist, approvals handled over email, reports assembled by hand in Excel. We build internal platforms, customer portals and management systems that follow the real flow of your operation, not the other way around.
The software is in your name from the first commit: repositories, database and infrastructure under your accounts, with no per-seat licenses that grow with your team.

challenge.heading: When generic software starts slowing operations down
points: The team runs critical processes in shared spreadsheets, with no permissions or change history.
You pay per-seat licenses for a tool you only use a fraction of, and it still lacks the features you need.
Information lives in several systems that don't talk to each other, and someone copies it by hand from one to the next.
Every small change depends on an outside vendor's roadmap.

deliverables: Complete source code in repositories under your name
A database modeled on your processes, with versioned migrations
Roles and permissions by user type, with an audit log
Automated deployment (CI/CD) on your own infrastructure
Technical and user documentation for your team

steps.title: Mapping the real process
steps.text: Before designing screens, we learn how work flows today: who does what, what gets approved, where time is lost and which data gets entered twice. That's where the data model comes from, not from a template.

steps.title: Phased scope
steps.text: We prioritize the module that frees up the most operational hours and ship it to production first. The rest is planned in phases with fixed dates and budgets, not a year-long project with no interim deliveries.

steps.title: Development with weekly progress
steps.text: Every week you get a private environment to test what's been built and give feedback directly to the engineers writing the code, with no middlemen.

steps.title: Launch and handover
steps.text: We migrate your existing data, train the team and hand over the documentation. During the 90-day warranty we fix any defect at no cost.

useCases: CRMs and customer portals built around your company's exact sales process, including follow-ups, proposals and invoicing.
Operations and logistics systems: dispatch, routing, inventory or real-time fleet tracking.
Internal tools that replace shared spreadsheets with a single database with permissions and traceability.
Multi-tenant SaaS platforms, when the software you build for yourself can also be sold to others.

faqs.question: Is it more expensive than paying for an existing tool?
faqs.answer: The upfront investment is higher, but there are no per-seat licenses growing every year and no features you pay for without using. It makes sense when your process is a differentiator, or when adapting a generic tool already costs more hours than building your own.

faqs.question: How long until it's in production?
faqs.answer: The first useful module usually ships in weeks, not months, because we work in phases. We set the exact timeline after mapping the process, with fixed dates in the contract.

faqs.question: What if I want to add features later?
faqs.answer: The code and documentation are yours, so you can keep working with us or with another team. The architecture is designed from the start to grow module by module without rewriting what already works.

related.label: How to choose a vendor without losing control of your code
related.description: What to require in the contract and in the repositories so the software is truly yours.

colombia.heading: Custom software development in Colombia
paragraphs: We work from Bogotá with companies across Colombia whose operations still rely on spreadsheets, email threads and generic tools they have outgrown. Because the team shares your time zone, process-mapping sessions and weekly demos are easy to schedule, and when a question comes up we reply within 24 business hours.

The software is designed around the local context from day one. If you handle personal data of customers or employees, role-based permissions, change history and the flows to answer data-subject requests are built to line up with Colombia's Law 1581 (Habeas Data). Connections to what you already use in the country, such as payment gateways or accounting systems, are planned during the initial mapping. Payment is split 50/50, the repositories are in your name from the first commit, and you get a 90-day technical warranty. Every phase ends with something usable in production, not a status report, so your team starts saving hours from the first module.
facts: Typical time to first launch: about {weeks.software} weeks

intro: A business mobile app isn't judged by how it looks in a demo, but by how it works out in the field: with poor signal, on a field technician's phone, or with thousands of customers opening it at once. We build iOS and Android apps with React Native, from a single codebase and with real offline mode.
We also handle publishing to the App Store and Google Play, including each store's review process, and the app is published under your developer accounts.

challenge.heading: What usually goes wrong in a business app
points: Field staff lose information when they drop signal and have to enter it again.
Maintaining two separate native apps doubles the cost of every change.
The app is published under the vendor's account and you have no control over updates.
The app doesn't connect to the internal system, so data gets transcribed by hand.

deliverables: An iOS and Android app from a single React Native codebase
Publishing on the App Store and Google Play under your accounts
A backend or integration with your existing systems
Offline sync with conflict resolution
Source code and a guide for publishing new versions

steps.title: Flows and context of use
steps.text: We define who uses the app, under what conditions (in the office, on the road, with no signal) and what they need to get done on each screen. That decides what works offline and what doesn't.

steps.title: Clickable prototype
steps.text: Before writing code, you validate a prototype of the main flows on your own phone. Fixing things there is far cheaper than in a version that's already published.

steps.title: Development with test builds
steps.text: You get installable test builds for iOS and Android every week, so your team can use them in real conditions before launch.

steps.title: Publishing and follow-up
steps.text: We prepare store listings, screenshots and compliance with each store's policies, publish the app and support you through the first weeks under the 90-day warranty.

useCases: Field apps for technicians, sales reps or drivers, with photo capture, signatures, GPS and offline mode.
Apps for end customers: scheduling, orders, service tracking or loyalty programs.
Apps that connect to device hardware, such as the camera, barcode scanner or Bluetooth.

faqs.question: Why React Native instead of separate native apps?
faqs.answer: With a single codebase for iOS and Android, each new feature is built and tested once, not twice. For the vast majority of business apps, performance is indistinguishable from a native app, and when a specific native module is needed, it integrates without issue.

faqs.question: Does the app work without internet?
faqs.answer: Yes, if the use case requires it. The app stores data locally and syncs it in the background when the signal returns, resolving conflicts if two people edited the same thing.

faqs.question: Who owns the app in the stores?
faqs.answer: You do. We publish under your Apple and Google developer accounts, and we hand over the code and the guide for publishing new versions.

colombia.heading: Mobile app development in Colombia
paragraphs: A business app in Colombia is used in conditions very unlike a demo: technicians where coverage is patchy, sales reps travelling between cities, customers opening it on a mid-range phone. That is why we start from how and where the app will be used and decide what must work offline. We build with React Native, one codebase for iOS and Android, so every feature is developed and tested once instead of twice.

We serve companies across the country by video call and send installable test builds every week, so your field team can try them in real conditions. We publish to the App Store and Google Play under your own developer accounts. If the app stores personal data of customers or staff, we apply the principles of Colombia's Law 1581 (Habeas Data): consent, a defined purpose and role-restricted access. After launch you have a 90-day technical warranty. If the app must also talk to your internal systems, the integration is scoped in the same plan rather than added as an afterthought.
facts: Typical time to first launch: about {weeks.mobile} weeks

intro: Most companies don't need another system: they need the ones they already have to talk to each other. We connect your software with payment gateways, accounting systems, ERPs and WhatsApp so information flows on its own, without anyone copying it from one screen to another.

We design every integration to fail safely: retries, a log of every event and alerts when an external provider doesn't respond. We explain the practices we apply in our [REST API architecture guide](/en/blog/buenas-practicas-apis-rest).

challenge.heading: Signs you're missing integrations
points: Someone on the team spends hours copying orders, payments or invoices from one system to another.
Online payments aren't automatically reconciled with accounting.
When an integration fails, nobody finds out until a customer complains.
Every new partner means building from scratch because there's no API of your own.

deliverables: Production integrations with retries and event logging
Signed and validated webhooks, never left open without authentication
Documentation of the API and of every data flow
Alerts when an external service fails or returns errors
Credentials and access under your accounts

steps.title: Data flow map
steps.text: We identify what information moves between systems, which system is the source of truth for each piece of data and what happens today when something fails.

steps.title: Contract design
steps.text: We define endpoints, formats and events before writing code, so each system knows exactly what it receives and what it returns.

steps.title: Resilient implementation
steps.text: Every integration includes idempotency (a repeated event doesn't duplicate a payment), retries with exponential backoff and signature validation on webhooks.

steps.title: Monitoring and documentation
steps.text: We leave a log of every event, alerts on failures and the documentation your team needs to understand and maintain each flow.

useCases: Payment gateways (Wompi, Stripe, PayU, Mercado Pago) automatically reconciled with your invoices.
Accounting systems and ERPs (Siigo, Alegra, SAP) synced with your sales or operations platform.
WhatsApp Cloud API for notifications, scheduling or automated customer service.
An API of your own so partners, customers or mobile apps can consume your data securely.

faqs.question: Can you integrate a system that has no API?
faqs.answer: Often, yes: through scheduled exports, controlled access to its database or, as a last resort, automating its user interface. We evaluate each case and tell you honestly how robust each option can be.

faqs.question: What happens if the external service goes down?
faqs.answer: Events are queued and retried automatically when the service comes back. If the failure persists, the system alerts the team instead of silently losing information.

faqs.question: Is it safe to connect payments and accounting data?
faqs.answer: Yes, with the right practices: encrypted credentials, webhooks with verified signatures, least-privilege permissions per integration and a log of every operation. It's part of the design, not an add-on at the end.

related.label: REST API architecture: 7 practices for production
related.description: Versioning, idempotency, error handling and other decisions that prevent outages.

colombia.heading: API and integration development in Colombia
paragraphs: The integrations Colombian companies usually need revolve around the same touchpoints: payment gateways such as Wompi, PayU or Mercado Pago, accounting systems such as Siigo or Alegra, ERPs such as SAP, and the WhatsApp Cloud API for notifications and customer service. From Bogotá we connect those systems to your platform for companies anywhere in the country, so an approved payment, an invoice or an order flows through on its own and nobody copies it from one screen to another.

Each integration is designed to fail safely: idempotency, retries with backoff, verified webhook signatures and a log of every event. Since these flows move customer data, we apply the principles of Colombia's Law 1581 (Habeas Data): only what is needed travels, with encrypted credentials and least-privilege permissions per integration. Credentials and access stay under your accounts, and you see progress in a test environment every week. If the system you want to connect has no API, we assess honestly how robust each alternative can be.
facts: Typical time to first launch: about {weeks.apis} weeks

intro: Site speed isn't a technical detail: it affects how many visitors stay, how many convert and how Google ranks you. We build websites and web applications with Next.js and React, designed at the architecture level to load fast, be accessible and get indexed well.
We measure with real tools (Lighthouse and Core Web Vitals) against the production build, not a development environment that produces misleading numbers.

Before writing code we set a performance budget: how much JavaScript each page may ship, the maximum weight of images and the range the Core Web Vitals must land in. Every design and development decision is checked against that budget, so speed is a condition of the project and not a last-minute adjustment.

challenge.heading: When your current site is costing you customers
points: The site loads slowly on mobile and visitors leave before they see the offer.
Core Web Vitals are in the red and organic rankings aren't improving.
Every content change requires a developer or breaks the design.
The site doesn't meet basic accessibility guidelines and excludes some of your users.

deliverables: A Next.js website or web application, deployed on your infrastructure
Green Core Web Vitals measured in production
Technical SEO: metadata, structured data, sitemap and per-language versions
Accessibility following WCAG guidelines
Source code and a guide for editing content
frontend-alto-rendimiento.stepsHeading: How we build a fast site

steps.title: Audit and goals
steps.text: We measure the current site (if there is one) and define what it needs to achieve: speed, conversion, rankings or all of the above. That sets the project's performance budget.

steps.title: Rendering architecture
steps.text: We decide what gets generated statically, what gets rendered on the server and what needs JavaScript in the browser. Shipping less JavaScript is the single biggest speed gain.

steps.title: Design and development
steps.text: We build with optimized images, lazy loading for whatever isn't in view and animations that don't compete with user interaction.

steps.title: Measurement in production
steps.text: We audit the real published version with Lighthouse and keep fixing until it meets the agreed targets before we call the project done.

useCases: Corporate websites and digital catalogs that need to rank in search engines.
Redesigns of slow sites without losing rankings or existing URLs.
Web applications with complex dashboards and forms that need to feel instant.
Multilingual sites with well-indexed per-language versions.

faqs.question: Will I lose my rankings if I redesign the site?
faqs.answer: Not if the migration is planned well. We keep the URLs that already rank or set up permanent redirects, and we preserve the metadata and content Google has already indexed.

faqs.question: Why Next.js?
faqs.answer: It lets you decide page by page what gets generated statically and what gets rendered on the server, which produces very fast, well-indexed sites without sacrificing dynamic functionality.

faqs.question: Will I be able to edit content without a developer?
faqs.answer: Yes. When the project calls for it, we integrate a content panel so your team can publish and edit without touching code.

faqs.question: What performance targets do you set?
faqs.answer: At a minimum, that all three Core Web Vitals land in the "good" range Google defines: Largest Contentful Paint (LCP) at 2.5 seconds or less, Interaction to Next Paint (INP) at 200 milliseconds or less and Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS) below 0.1. They are measured on the published version under mobile conditions, not on a developer machine.

faqs.question: How much does a website or web application cost, and how long does it take?
faqs.answer: As a reference, a website starts at {priceUsd.web} and is typically ready in about {weeks.web} weeks. The final price depends on scope, integrations and the modules you add: the [estimator](/en/cotizador) calculates an approximate value and timeline in minutes, and we give the definitive quote after talking with you, with no commitment.

faqs.question: How do you handle images, fonts and third-party scripts?
faqs.answer: They are the three usual culprits behind a slow site. Images are generated in several sizes and modern formats and loaded only when they are about to be seen; fonts are served from your own site with controlled loading to avoid layout shifts; and third-party scripts (analytics, chat widgets, pixels) load deferred and, where it applies, only after the visitor consents.

faqs.question: Can you build and index a multilingual website?
faqs.answer: Yes. Each language version needs its own URL, hreflang annotations and metadata, so that every version can rank in its own market and search engines understand how the versions relate. This site is itself published in Spanish, English and French, with each page adapted to its language rather than copied.

faqs.question: What happens to performance after launch?
faqs.answer: A fast site can degrade with every change: one unoptimized image or a new script is enough. With Search Console you can follow the real data of your visitors in the Core Web Vitals report. After launch you get a 90-day technical warranty and, if you want ongoing support, you can optionally contract maintenance with a custom SLA.

colombia.heading: Web development for international teams, built from Bogotá, Colombia
paragraphs: If your team is in the United States or Europe, working with a studio in Bogotá is less distant than it sounds. Colombia stays on UTC−5 all year with no daylight saving shift, so our working day matches US Eastern Time in winter, runs one hour behind it in summer and overlaps with the European afternoon during Bogotá's morning. We work and write in English, Spanish and French, and you talk directly to the engineers who build your site.

We build high-performance websites and web applications with Next.js and React, measured with Lighthouse and Core Web Vitals on the published version. Multilingual sites ship with their own URLs, hreflang annotations and metadata per language, as this site does. Forms and analytics are built around visitor consent, in line with GDPR and CCPA expectations, although legal compliance still needs your counsel. Payment is split 50% at signing and 50% on delivery, and the code and repositories are in your name from day one.
facts: Typical time to first launch: about {weeks.web} weeks

intro: Generic e-commerce platforms are a good way to start, but as sales grow, transaction fees, payment plugins and catalog limitations start to weigh on you. We build custom stores with no per-sale fees, connected directly to your inventory, your invoicing and your shipping carriers.

challenge.heading: When your store's platform starts holding you back
points: You pay fees on every sale on top of the monthly subscription and plugins.
The catalog doesn't support your actual variants, attributes or pricing rules.
The store's inventory doesn't match the warehouse, and you sell products that are out of stock.
Checkout has too many steps and doesn't offer the payment methods your customers use.

deliverables: A custom online store with no per-sale fees
A catalog with variants, attributes and synced stock
Checkout with local and international payment gateways
Integration with shipping carriers and invoicing
An admin panel for orders, products and inventory

steps.title: Catalog and business rules
steps.text: We model your products, variants, prices, discounts and taxes the way they actually work in your business, not the way a template imposes them.

steps.title: Checkout and payments
steps.text: We design a short checkout and connect the gateways your customers use, with payment confirmation verified on the server, never only in the browser.

steps.title: Inventory and logistics
steps.text: We sync stock with your system or warehouse and connect shipping carriers to generate shipping labels and tracking automatically.

steps.title: Launch and optimization
steps.text: We launch with conversion analytics and support you through the first weeks to tune the funnel with real data.

useCases: Fashion and footwear brands with many size and color variants per product.
Stores migrating from a generic platform to eliminate fees and gain control.
B2B businesses with customer-specific price lists, minimum orders or online quoting.

faqs.question: Should I go with a custom store or a platform like Shopify?
faqs.answer: To start selling quickly, a generic platform is usually enough. A custom store makes sense when fees, plugins or catalog limitations already cost more than building your own would.

faqs.question: What payment methods can I offer?
faqs.answer: We integrate local and international gateways such as Wompi, PayU, Mercado Pago and Stripe, with cards, bank transfers and other methods each gateway supports in your country.

faqs.question: Can I migrate my products and customers from my current store?
faqs.answer: Yes. We migrate your catalog, customers and order history, and set up redirects so your product pages don't lose their rankings.

colombia.heading: E-commerce and online store development in Colombia
paragraphs: An online store in Colombia is won or lost at checkout: which payment methods it offers, how quickly it confirms payment and how it connects to inventory and shipping. From Bogotá we build custom stores for companies across the country, with gateways such as Wompi, PayU, Mercado Pago or Stripe, payment confirmation verified on the server and stock synced with your system or warehouse, without the per-sale commissions of a third-party platform.

If you sell on a generic platform today, we migrate your catalog, customers and order history and set up redirects so your product pages keep their search ranking. Because a store holds buyers' personal data, registration and checkout are designed with processing authorization and flows to answer data-subject requests, in line with Colombia's Law 1581 (Habeas Data). Payment is split 50/50, the code is 100% yours and you get a 90-day technical warranty. After launch we help tune the funnel with real conversion data during the first weeks.

intro: Security isn't added at the end of a project: it's decided in the architecture. We implement role-based access control, encryption of sensitive information and audit logging from the design stage, and we align the software with data protection regulations such as Colombia's Law 1581 and the GDPR in Europe.
We explain it in detail in our [technical guide to Law 1581](/en/blog/ley-1581-guia-tecnica-software): what the law requires and how it translates into concrete software decisions.

challenge.heading: Risks we often find in an audit
points: Every internal user sees all the data, with no role-based permissions.
Passwords or personal data stored unencrypted or in application logs.
There's no way to know who changed a record or when.
There's no process for responding when a data subject requests their data or asks for it to be deleted.

deliverables: An audit report with risks prioritized according to OWASP
Role-based access control and audit logging
Encryption of sensitive data at rest and in transit
Workflows for exercising the rights of access, portability and erasure
Technical documentation of the measures implemented
seguridad-cumplimiento.stepsHeading: How we approach your software's security

steps.title: Initial audit
steps.text: We review code, configuration and infrastructure against the most common vulnerabilities (OWASP Top 10) and map what personal data you handle and where it lives.

steps.title: Prioritized remediation plan
steps.text: We rank each finding by impact and effort, so you fix what poses a real risk first and don't spend budget on cosmetic issues.

steps.title: Implementing controls
steps.text: We apply role-based permissions, encryption, strong authentication (including two-factor), audit logging and limits against brute-force attacks.

steps.title: Documented compliance
steps.text: We document the technical measures and the processes for handling data subject requests, as evidence for an audit or a regulatory inquiry.

useCases: Companies that handle customers' personal data and need to align with Law 1581 or the GDPR.
Platforms about to go through an audit or due diligence by a client or investor.
Legacy systems that need to be modernized without exposing sensitive information: see [legacy system migration](/en/servicios/migracion-datos-legacy).

faqs.question: Do you issue compliance certifications?
faqs.answer: We're not a certification body. We implement the technical measures the regulations require and document them, so your company has solid evidence for an audit or for the data protection authority.

faqs.question: Can you audit a system you didn't build?
faqs.answer: Yes. The audit covers the existing code and infrastructure regardless of who built them, and the report includes a prioritized remediation plan.

faqs.question: Which regulations do you cover?
faqs.answer: We work from the technical requirements of Colombia's Law 1581 and the European GDPR, which share principles such as consent, data minimization and data subject rights, and we use OWASP as our application security reference.

related.label: Law 1581 in practice: what your software needs to do
related.description: The law's requirements translated into concrete development decisions.

colombia.heading: Security and Law 1581 compliance in Colombia
paragraphs: Colombia's Law 1581 of 2012 (Habeas Data) requires anyone processing personal data in the country to obtain authorization, limit the purpose and answer data-subject requests, and the Superintendence of Industry and Commerce oversees compliance. From Bogotá we help companies across Colombia turn those principles into concrete technical measures: role-based access control, encryption, audit logging and flows to handle access, update and deletion requests.

If your company also serves users in Europe, we align the controls with the GDPR, which shares principles such as consent, minimization and data-subject rights, and we use the OWASP Top 10 as the reference for auditing code. The audit works the same on systems we did not build. We are not a certification body: we deliver the implemented measures and their documentation as evidence for an audit or a regulatory request. We start with an audit of the code and the data, and a remediation plan prioritized by real risk. We work with weekly progress updates and reply within 24 business hours.

challenge.heading: Signs your software depends on a single person
points: Nobody at the company has admin access to the repositories, servers or domains.
Deploying a change requires one specific person to do it by hand.
There's no diagram of how the systems connect or where the credentials are.

Automated deployment pipelines (CI/CD)
An inventory of services, environment variables and access
Setup, operations and maintenance guides

intro: A legacy system isn't just old software: it's the one still running your billing, inventory or daily operations, yet nobody dares to change it. Our legacy software migration service replaces it module by module, with the old system running in parallel until the new one proves it processes the same transactions with the same results.

We don't do weekend "big bang" cutovers. We use the Strangler Fig pattern, data synchronization between both systems and automated reconciliation before every cutover, all explained in our [guide to legacy system migration without downtime](/en/blog/migracion-sistemas-legados-sin-interrupcion).

challenge.heading: Signs your system has already become legacy
points: Every small change takes weeks because nobody dares to touch the code.
Only one person understands how it works, and their absence brings operations to a halt.
The vendor or the technology no longer has support or security updates.
The system can't be integrated with the tools the business needs today.

deliverables: A new platform in production, module by module
Versioned, repeatable data migration scripts
A reconciliation report between the legacy system and the new one
A read-only archive of the historical data that must be retained
Documentation of the new architecture and the cutover processes
migracion-datos-legacy.stepsHeading: How we migrate a legacy system with zero downtime

steps.title: System and data assessment
steps.text: We inventory modules, integrations, scheduled jobs and business rules buried in code or stored procedures, and we measure data volume, quality and duplicates before committing to a timeline.

steps.title: Per-module decision: migrate, retain or retire
steps.text: Not everything deserves a rewrite. Each module is classified as rehost, refactor, replace with SaaS, wrap behind an API or retire, so the budget goes where the legacy system actually slows the business down.

steps.title: Target architecture and routing layer
steps.text: We design the new platform plus an intermediate layer that decides which requests the old system serves and which the new one does. That's what makes an incremental migration possible without users switching tools every week.

steps.title: Phased data migration
steps.text: Extraction, cleansing, deduplication and schema mapping with versioned, repeatable scripts. Both systems stay in sync while they coexist, so there's never a day when the data is "half migrated".

steps.title: Validation and reconciliation
steps.text: Before every cutover we compare record counts, totals and critical records between the legacy and the new system, and run regression tests on business workflows. If the numbers don't match, the cutover doesn't happen.

steps.title: Cutover, monitoring and decommissioning
steps.text: Traffic moves gradually and reversibly, we monitor errors and performance, and only at the end do we decommission the old system, keeping a read-only archive of the historical data you're legally required to retain.

useCases: A custom ERP or line-of-business app built 10-15 years ago, undocumented, with a single person who understands the code.
Operations running on scattered Excel spreadsheets, XML files or Access databases that need a single database with permissions and audit trails.
Desktop applications (Visual Basic, Delphi, legacy PHP) that must move to the web or the cloud without stopping invoicing.

Databases that don't meet today's data protection requirements (GDPR, CCPA) and need encryption, access control and auditing: see our [security and compliance](/en/servicios/seguridad-cumplimiento) service.
Systems that must be retired without migrating the full history: only active data moves, the rest stays in a read-only archive.

faqs.question: How long does a legacy system migration take?
faqs.answer: It depends on the number of modules and the state of the data. A well-scoped module with clean data can reach production in weeks; a full ERP is planned in phases over several months. Each phase ships value and is reversible, so you don't wait until the end to use the new system.

faqs.question: Can we migrate without downtime?
faqs.answer: Yes, that's the whole point of a phased migration. The legacy system keeps running while the new one takes over module by module, with data synchronized between them. Each cutover is gradual and can be rolled back if something fails.

faqs.question: What happens to our historical data?
faqs.answer: It's audited before anything moves. Data used in daily operations is cleansed and migrated with integrity checks; data kept only for legal or accounting reasons can live in a read-only archive instead of being loaded into the new system.

faqs.question: Should we migrate or keep maintaining the current system?
faqs.answer: Migrate when the cost of keeping it (hours per change, outages, no vendor support, security exposure) exceeds the cost of modernizing it, or when it blocks integrations the business needs. If the system is stable and blocks no one, wrapping it behind an API and leaving it alone is sometimes the right call.

faqs.question: Who owns the code and documentation?
faqs.answer: You do. The code is 100% yours from day one, and we hand over the architecture documentation and the migration scripts so your team can maintain the new system without depending on us.

colombia.heading: Legacy system migration and modernization in Colombia
paragraphs: Many Colombian companies still run on a custom ERP built over a decade ago, a desktop application or Excel workbooks that carry invoicing and inventory. From Bogotá we migrate those systems in phases for companies across the country: the old system keeps running in parallel while the new one takes over module by module, with data kept in sync and a reconciliation before every cutover, with no weekend shutdowns.

A migration is also a personal-data topic: before moving anything we audit what sensitive information exists and where, and the new database ships with encryption, access control and auditing aligned with Colombia's Law 1581 (Habeas Data). Records the law requires you to keep for accounting or tax reasons can stay in a read-only archive instead of being loaded into the new system. The code and the migration scripts are yours from day one, and you get a 90-day technical warranty after the final cutover. If a module is stable and slows nobody down, we may recommend wrapping it behind an API instead of rewriting it.

intro: Useful AI for a business isn't a generic chatbot: it's a model connected to your documents, your systems and your processes that solves a specific, measurable task. We implement assistants, automated data extraction and semantic search over your company's information.
We always start with a narrowly scoped use case, with a clear metric for hours saved or errors avoided, before scaling to more processes.

challenge.heading: Tasks that typically eat up the team's hours
points: Manually keying in data from invoices, orders or scanned documents.
Answering the same customer questions over and over on WhatsApp or email.
Hunting for information scattered across documents, manuals and old conversations.
Sorting and routing incoming requests before anyone can handle them.

deliverables: A use case implemented and connected to your systems
An assistant or automation with answers grounded in your own data
Privacy controls over what information is sent to the model
A dashboard or log to review and correct what the AI does
Impact measurement against the agreed baseline
inteligencia-artificial-aplicada.stepsHeading: How we implement AI in your operation

steps.title: Choosing the use case
steps.text: We identify a repetitive task with enough volume and a verifiable outcome. If AI isn't the best tool for that problem, we tell you.

steps.title: Testing with your data
steps.text: We build a proof of concept with real documents and cases from your company to measure accuracy before investing in the full version.

steps.title: Integration and controls
steps.text: We connect the solution to your systems and channels, with human review at critical points and clear rules about what data leaves your infrastructure.

steps.title: Measurement and improvement
steps.text: We measure the results against the baseline and fine-tune using the cases where the model got it wrong.

useCases: Assistants on WhatsApp or internal channels that answer with your company's actual information.
Automated data extraction from invoices, purchase orders and scanned documents.
Semantic search across manuals, policies and the internal knowledge base.
Automatic classification and routing of support or sales requests.

faqs.question: Is my data used to train third-party models?
faqs.answer: We use providers and configurations that don't train on data sent through the API, we limit the information that reaches the model to what's strictly necessary, and we document what data leaves your infrastructure.

faqs.question: What happens when the AI gets it wrong?
faqs.answer: That's why we design human review at critical points and a log of every response. Errors are used to fine-tune the system, and for sensitive tasks the AI proposes and a person approves.

faqs.question: Do I need my data organized before we start?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily. Part of the work is preparing and structuring the information. The proof of concept quickly reveals whether the data quality is good enough or needs work first.

colombia.heading: Applied artificial intelligence development in Colombia
paragraphs: Artificial intelligence worth having in a Colombian company solves one concrete task: answering on WhatsApp with real information from the business, extracting data from scanned invoices and purchase orders, or searching internal manuals and policies. From Bogotá we serve companies across the country and always start with a narrow use case, a clear metric and a proof of concept on your own documents before investing in the full version.

The data that feeds a model often includes customer information, so we apply Colombia's Law 1581 (Habeas Data) from the design stage: only what is strictly necessary reaches the model, we use providers and settings that do not train on data received through the API, and we document what information leaves your infrastructure. At critical points a person reviews and approves what the AI proposes. You see results in a test environment every week and we reply within 24 business hours. If AI is not the best tool for the problem, we tell you before you invest.
